title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.39 (versions follow prime numbers; 139 after 137): what is written to her, as it is. Luma's dialogue no longer hangs on a long line: the visible tail of the line was computed with a wrong sign, so past 25 letters she read before her own room and the kernel stopped her. The kernel now delivers every typed character (event 7: its Unicode code point, surrogate pairs joined) besides the key that produced it, and Luma keeps it as UTF-8. A letter, for her, is a..z or any whole character past ASCII, its print being its own code point: which accented forms are the same is not given to her in a table, by the author's decision; she is to learn it from what she reads, since her judge is compression. Two places where the dialogue and the letter drawing used her digestion's memory as scratch were moved to their own room. The kernel test suite: 411 passing, 0 failing. Stated limits: she has not yet learned that accented and plain letters are one; letters missing from her 5x7 dot alphabet show as an empty cell; any character past ASCII counts as a letter, punctuation included; event 7 has no dedicated kernel test yet. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.39: a Luma se le escribe con acentos, eñes y emojis, sin colgarse; qué letras valen lo mismo lo aprende ella. Prototipo de investigación.
